thank you. Hey, we're here to talk about health care, though, and in particular, mental health care. You have some, there's new rules from the abided administration that would strengthen and reinforce laws, according to the information that I have here. I tell you what, why don't you tell us about that?

Well, so for over 15 years, it's been the law in this country that insurance companies need to cover people's mental health care needs, just like they do physical health care. That's the law. And we have Minnesota Senator Paul Wellstone to thank for that. He passed this law and championed it, you know, as I said, over 15 years ago. But I think we also know that for years, insurance companies have been finding ways to get around this law. And I've been working to fix these loopholes since I came to the Senate. So this is why it's so important that the President Biden and Vice President Harris put out this new rule in the last week to tighten up and close these loopholes. And I'm just really grateful for that. I think we all know what insurance companies can do with mental health care treatment. They will do prior authorizations that make it almost impossible to get care. They will require you to go through different steps of care, even though your doctor has said that you need step C, they say no, you have to do step A and B first. They just throw up a lot of barriers. And so this new rule will increase the price that insurance companies pay for going through that and will require them to drop some of that red tape. So it's a big deal and I'm excited that they've made this headway.

turn_text: Now this is according to the information I have. This is a new rule as opposed to a brand new bill or anything. So it's just strengthening. I guess does it need support in the Senate and in the House?

Well, I think there's still more to do. This rule can go into effect under President Biden or President Harris without any additional congressional action, which is a really good thing. And this goes to show how the way our government works is if you have very strong purpose and accountability at the top, then the agencies will do the hard work of making sure that these laws are followed. And if you don't, then it can be a very different situation. But I do want to say that I think that we need tougher laws as well. And it would require an act of Congress to force insurance companies to pay financial penalties, for example, if they weren't providing parity between mental health care and physical health care. And so those are some of the laws that I think that we should continue to push for to get the kind of accountability that we need.

We're talking once again with Senator Tina Smith. We're talking about mental health care and how treatment is covered by insurance companies. Will there be still further issues? Mental health is such a big issue in this day and age. We all know somebody, if not ourselves, that have been at times either suffer from some type of anxiety or depression or something. So it's such a big thing. Are there further things down the road that we will need to do?

There absolutely is more that we need to do. And I always being an optimist think that one of the silver linings of the pandemic is that it has raised awareness of the how many Americans experience some challenge with mental health in their lifetimes. And it has particularly drawn our attention to the challenges that younger people have as an example. So yes, there is a lot more that we need to do. A couple of things that I am working on is one is to try to increase the number of people that are going into the field of mental health care. So a challenge is that when you get ready to go and find somebody to help you, it can be quite difficult. In rural counties in particular, struggle, there might be only one or two or even no providers in those communities. So helping people to get the training and the training that they need so that they can move into the field is really important. Another thing that's important is to continue to support access to tele-mental health, which is something that we started doing during the pandemic. And it has been a real godsend for people who find that in some cases it's better for them to be able to do a video call with a therapist or a counselor rather than having to leave the house and drive long distances which might just not be practical for them. So those are two additional things that I think would help expand access to mental health care.
